key_insight: Entropy estimation in multi-qutrit systems shifts from VQA-based methods for small systems to CNN-based estimation for larger systems, with performance driven mainly by trainable parameter count and sufficient entanglement.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a scalable workflow for quantum entropy estimation: use hardware-efficient variational circuits for up to three qutrits and measurement-based CNNs for larger systems when full tomography is impractical.
method: Evaluated 11 SU(3)-inspired, hardware-efficient VQA ansatzes for up to three qutrits.
Trained a CNN on tensor-product mutually unbiased basis measurement outcomes for two to five qutrits.
Compared performance under ideal simulation, shot noise, and out-of-distribution states.
evidence_signal: In simulation, about 12.5% of tomography measurements were enough for the CNN to reach 90th-percentile absolute errors of roughly 0.13–0.16 nats for four- and five-qutrit systems, with error decreasing as system size increased.
watch_item: Results are based on an ideal quantum simulator, so hardware noise, calibration errors, and scalability to real devices may alter performance.
paper_title: Entropy Estimation in Multi-Qutrit Systems via Variational and Classical Neural Networks
